The defined implementation codes leave numeric gaps with no assigned symbol after L1 invalidate and inside L2 encodings and around unaligned branch and exception encodings and between RC and L3 blocks, so the sequence from hex 40 to hex A8 is not contiguous.

ARMV8_PMU_PMCR_E is bit 0 for master enable, ARMV8_PMU_PMCR_P is bit 1 for global reset, ARMV8_PMU_PMCR_C is bit 2 for cycle reset, ARMV8_PMU_PMCR_D is bit 3 for divide by 64 cycle counting, ARMV8_PMU_PMCR_X is bit 4 for trace export, ARMV8_PMU_PMCR_DP is bit 5 for debug suppression of cycle counting, ARMV8_PMU_PMCR_LC is bit 6 for wide cycle overflow, ARMV8_PMU_PMCR_LP is bit 7 for wide event counters, ARMV8_PMU_PMCR_N occupies bits 11 through 15 for counter count.

The PMCR mask unions the eight single bit controls for enable reset cycle divide export debug long cycle and long event while excluding the multibit counter count field, defining which control bits are considered writable by the owning logic.
ARMV8_PMU_OVSR_P covers bits 0 through 30 for event overflow, ARMV8_PMU_OVSR_C is bit 31 for cycle overflow, ARMV8_PMU_OVSR_F is bit 32 as a wide 64 bit value valid on arm64 only.
The overflowed mask is the union of the event range mask, the cycle bit and the arm64 only fault bit, providing a single test for any counter overflow condition.

ARMV8_PMU_EVTYPE_EVENT covers bits 0 through 15 for event code, ARMV8_PMU_EVTYPE_TH covers bits 32 through 43 as a wide mask on arm64 only, ARMV8_PMU_EVTYPE_TC covers bits 61 through 63 as a wide mask on arm64 only.

ARMV8_PMU_USERENR_EN is bit 0 for EL0 register access, ARMV8_PMU_USERENR_SW is bit 1 for EL0 software increment write, ARMV8_PMU_USERENR_CR is bit 2 for EL0 cycle read, ARMV8_PMU_USERENR_ER is bit 3 for EL0 event read, ARMV8_PMU_USERENR_UEN is bit 4 for fine grained per counter EL0 access.
The user enable mask unions EN SW CR and ER while omitting UEN, so the fine grained control is managed separately from the coarse enable mask.

A dispatch helper provides one case for each integer from 0 through 30 inclusive that runs a caller chosen per index action then exits, while any other index produces a warning about an invalid selector, bounding valid event register indices to 31 values.
The performance header defines a unique guard macro that prevents repeated inclusion within a single translation unit.

Callchain entry holds nr as an eight byte count followed by ip as a flexible list of eight byte addresses whose bound comes from a max stack control. Callchain context holds entry pointer with max_stack and nr as 32 bit limits with contexts as a short tag and contexts_maxed as a boolean saturation flag. The copy callback type returns an unsigned length and accepts at least a destination pointer and a const source pointer, with remaining signature outside the visible range.

Raw fragment overlays next pointer with pad word in shared storage then orders copy callback with data pointer and size as 32 bit, marked to suppress padding. Raw record orders frag then size as 32 bit total. The helper named perf_raw_frag_last reports final fragment when pad is numerically less than the width of eight bytes.
Branch stack orders nr as eight byte count with hw_idx as eight byte hardware position then entries as a flexible list of branch records.
Extra register descriptor orders config as 64 bit value with reg as unsigned address, alloc as integer allocation flag and idx as integer position inside shared register storage.

When perf support is configured the hardware event state opens with an overlay where one view is live. The hardware view sequences config config1 last_tag and dyn_constraint as 64 bit, config_base and event_base as unsigned long, event_base_rdpmc idx last_cpu and flags as integers, plus extra_reg and branch_reg as extra descriptors. The aux view holds aux_config as 64 bit with aux_paused as unsigned that may change asynchronously. The software view holds hrtimer. The tracepoint view holds tp_list. The power view holds pwr_acc and ptsc as 64 bit. The conditional breakpoint view holds info with bp_list. The iommu view holds iommu_bank and iommu_cntr as bytes with padding plus conf and conf1 as 64 bit.

After the opening overlay the same state orders target task pointer with addr_filters opaque pointer and addr_filters_gen unsigned generation, state as integer, prev_count as 64 bit atomic, sample_period as 64 bit, a second overlay, interrupts_seq with interrupts as 64 bit throttle counters, plus freq_time_stamp with freq_count_stamp as 64 bit frequency markers.

PERF_HES_STOPPED is bit 0 for stopped counter, PERF_HES_UPTODATE is bit 1 for fresh count, PERF_HES_ARCH is bit 2 for arch use. The second overlay selects sampling with last_period as 64 bit and period_left as 64 bit atomic allowing periods beyond hardware limits, or topdown with saved_metric and saved_slots for context switch. Prev count tolerates nested reads via atomic compare exchange, sample period seeds the next sample, and aux paused cannot merge into state because it updates asynchronously.

The PMU descriptor orders entry list node with events_lock spinlock guarding events list, module with dev and parent pointers, attr_groups with attr_update tables, name string with type integer, capabilities flags with scope value, cpu_pmu_context per cpu pointer, exclusive_cnt atomic where negative means cpu bound and positive means task bound, task_ctx_nr with hrtimer_interval_ms and nr_addr_filters counts, plus task_ctx_cache slab pointer for task context storage.

Optional pmu_enable and pmu_disable bracket wide activity for interrupt safety and batched writes. Event_init validates ownership and returns distinct negatives for not for this PMU, missing device, busy, invalid, unsupported and privilege failures with zero on success. Optional event_mapped and event_unmapped observe address space attach with event and memory descriptor. Optional event_idx supplies mmap index defaulting to zero. Sched_task receives PMU context with task and direction on switch. Optional setup_aux builds private aux state from event pages count and overwrite flag, released by optional free_aux.

Add reserves hardware for an event with flags and del releases it, read refreshes the software count and for sampling also refreshes remaining period, start and stop control counting with flags, while optional start_txn opens a group transaction that defers schedulability checks, commit_txn closes it on success or leaves it open on failure, and cancel_txn aborts it assuming del for each prior add.

PERF_EF_START is hex 1 to start on add, PERF_EF_RELOAD is hex 2 to reprogram on start, PERF_EF_UPDATE is hex 4 to save count on stop, PERF_EF_PAUSE is hex 8 for minimal aux pause, PERF_EF_RESUME is hex 10 for minimal aux resume. Add without start equals add then stop, del always updates, stop with update behaves like read, start with reload must follow stop with update, pause and resume never overlap themselves but may overlap other start stop pairs. Add del start and stop run with interrupts disabled and local PMU quiet, with start and stop additionally tolerating nonmaskable interrupt context.

A dedicated spinlock guards the per PMU event list against concurrent add and delete, while hardware programming paths execute with local interrupts disabled and the PMU disabled on the current processor, and overflow continuations rely on stop in interrupt context followed by start to resume.

Flexible address and branch lists require explicit bounds from count and max depth to avoid overflow. Packed raw storage and overlaid event views demand single view discipline and alignment care. Asynchronous aux pause with nested counter reads and group transaction rollback require atomic updates with idempotent stop and del paths. Absent optional hooks must be null checked and nonmaskable reachable start stop paths must avoid blocking.
